title: Your MOS form, field by field
sub: In MOS order. Tap a value to copy it, then paste it into MOS yourself.
loadFailed: Your case could not be loaded, so nothing is prefilled. The field list below is still complete.
ready: {ready} of {total} fields ready from your case
sourceNote: Field list from the official form, {regulation} ({link}), in force from {inForce}, checked {checked}. The MOS screens may word some labels slightly differently. Dossierly never logs in to MOS or files for you.
openMos: Open MOS in a new tab
sourceUnconfirmed: Source (not confirmed in an official text)
regTitle: Is your university or employer real and active?
regSub: Checked live against the Ministry of Finance white list and the National Court Register (KRS).
regInvalid: Enter a 10-digit NIP (tax number) or a KRS number.
fillingRule: The application is filled in Polish (instruction 2). Where you have no data, choose "brak" (none) instead of leaving a required field empty (instruction 3).
h.A.1: Surname exactly as in the passport, in Latin letters.
h.A.4: All given names as in the passport.
h.A.9: Year, month, day. If no document shows it, enter the probable year of birth (instruction 4).
h.A.10: Enter M for male or K for female (instruction 5). K is the Polish letter for kobieta, not for "F".
h.A.11: Town of birth as in the passport.
h.A.13: Write your nationality in Polish, lower case.
h.A.15: Use one of: panna, kawaler, mężatka, żonaty, rozwiedziona, rozwiedziony, wdowa, wdowiec (instruction 5).
h.A.16: Highest education completed, in Polish (for example podstawowe, średnie, wyższe).
h.A.18: 11 digits if you already have a PESEL, otherwise "brak".
h.A.19: A number where the office can reach you, with country code.
h.A.20: An address you read daily: MOS sends the signing link and the certificate here.
h.B.I.2: State or province, as written on your documents.
h.B.I.3: District, or "brak" if your country has none.
h.B.I.9: Postal code in the local format.
h.B.II.1: Country name in Polish. Only if you lived in another country before.
h.B.II.2: State or province, as written on your documents. Only if you lived in another country before.
h.B.II.3: District, or "brak" if your country has none. Only if you lived in another country before.
h.B.II.4: Municipality or city council, or "brak". Only if you lived in another country before.
h.B.II.5: Town or city. Only if you lived in another country before.
h.B.II.6: Street name, or "brak". Only if you lived in another country before.
h.B.II.7: House or building number. Only if you lived in another country before.
h.B.II.8: Flat number, or "brak". Only if you lived in another country before.
h.B.II.9: Postal code in the local format. Only if you lived in another country before.
h.C.series: Series letters if the passport has any; many do not, then "brak".
h.C.authority: Authority name and country, as printed.
l.C.others: Number of other persons entered in the travel document
h.C.others: 0 unless children are entered in your passport.
s.D: D. Where you live in Poland
h.D.1: Voivodeship of your address in Poland.
h.D.2: Powiat. For Warsaw it is m. st. Warszawa.
h.D.5: Street as in your rental agreement or dormitory registration.
h.E.I: Choose exactly one purpose. For a student it is option 6, the studies option. Your university completes Annex 5 for it.
h.E.II: Name, sex, date of birth, kinship, citizenship, residence, whether they apply for a permit and whether you support them. Write "brak" if none.
l.E.III.a: Previous stays in Poland (periods and legal basis)
h.E.III.a: Earlier stays with dates and basis (visa, permit, visa-free). "brak" if this is your first.
h.E.III.b.1: Tak if you are in Poland now. You must file no later than the last day of your legal stay (art. 105 ust. 1 of the Act).
l.E.III.b.2: Date of your last entry to Poland
h.E.III.b.2: Year, month, day. Check the stamp in your passport.
l.E.III.b.3: On what basis are you in Poland now?
h.E.III.b.3: Tick one: ruchu bezwizowego, wizy, zezwolenia na pobyt czasowy, or dokumentu uprawniającego do wjazdu i pobytu wydanego przez inne państwo obszaru Schengen. A student on a national study visa ticks wizy; someone extending an earlier permit ticks zezwolenia na pobyt czasowy.
l.E.IV: Trips and stays abroad outside Poland in the last 5 years
h.E.IV: Country and period for each stay abroad, last 5 years.
l.E.V: Financial means to cover your living costs
h.E.V: Monthly amount and source (family support, scholarship, work). The Act requires means above the social-assistance income threshold after housing costs, plus return travel and study costs (art. 144 ust. 1 pkt 2 lit. b, ust. 1a).
h.E.VI: Insurer, policy number and validity. NFZ cover or private cover of treatment costs in Poland both qualify (art. 144 ust. 1 pkt 2 lit. a).
l.E.VII: Are you detained, in a guarded centre, banned from leaving the country, serving a prison sentence or in pre-trial detention?
h.E.VII: Answer for yourself truthfully. Answer Tak (yes) or Nie (no); if you answer Tak, a detail box opens.
l.E.VIII: Have you been convicted by a court in Poland?
h.E.VIII: Only convictions in Poland. Answer Tak (yes) or Nie (no); if you answer Tak, a detail box opens.
l.E.IX: Are criminal or petty-offence proceedings pending against you in Poland?
h.E.IX: Include fines you contest. Answer Tak (yes) or Nie (no); if you answer Tak, a detail box opens.
l.E.X: Do you owe obligations from court rulings or administrative decisions, including maintenance, in Poland or abroad?
h.E.X: Includes unpaid maintenance and unpaid administrative fines. Answer Tak (yes) or Nie (no); if you answer Tak, a detail box opens.
h.F.1: Two or three Polish sentences: your programme, university, and the period you need the permit for. Keep it factual.
l.G.1: I declare the data in the application is true.
h.G.1: A statement you make yourself. Dossierly never ticks or signs this for you.
l.G.2: I am aware of criminal liability for a false statement.
l.G.sign: Qualified electronic signature, personal signature or trusted signature
h.G.sign: You sign personally in MOS through login.gov.pl. The application cannot be signed by a proxy; it is only unlocked after your university completes its annex.
a.photo.title: Passport-style photo (digital file)
a.photo.detail: Colour, sharp, face 70-80% of the frame, plain light background, facing the camera, eyes open and visible, mouth closed, no head covering or dark glasses (exceptions need a signed statement). Taken within 6 months before you file.
a.photo.spec: JPG file, at least 684 x 883 px (width x height), at most 2.5 MB, proportions of a 35 x 45 mm photo.
a.passport.title: Digital copy of every page of your passport
a.passport.detail: All pages, including blank ones and the cover if the office needs it. If you have no valid passport and cannot get one, another identity document replaces it.
a.passport.spec: Scan or photo saved as PDF. Each file at most 10 MB, all files together at most 50 MB.
a.university_certificate.title: Annex 5, completed and signed by your university (replaces the paper certificate)
a.university_certificate.detail: You give your university's e-mail address in the application. MOS sends the university a link; an authorised person fills in the study dates, programme, level, fees and language, and signs it electronically. You cannot sign and send your own application until the university has finished. Ask the international office early, because you cannot file until it is done.
a.stamp_duty_proof.title: Proof of payment of the stamp duty
a.stamp_duty_proof.detail: A bank transfer confirmation or scan. You pay outside MOS to the voivodeship's account, with the permit type and your name as the title.
a.stamp_duty_proof.spec: PDF or image of the confirmation.
a.stamp_duty_proof.note: UdSC says the stamp duty is the only application cost. Whether the proof must be uploaded at filing or only when the voivode calls for payment (art. 106e ust. 2 mentions such a call) differs between office notices, so check your voivodeship's current MOS instructions before paying.
a.card_fee_proof.title: Proof of payment of the residence card fee
a.card_fee_proof.detail: Paid to a UdSC account with a title naming you. A 50% reduction exists for people in difficult financial circumstances.
a.card_fee_proof.note: UdSC lists the card fee as a cost of the procedure. The Poznań voivodeship office says the card fee need not be paid before the decision, so timing differs between sources.
a.health_insurance.title: Health insurance policy
a.health_insurance.detail: The Act requires you to have NFZ-type insurance or an insurer's confirmation that it covers treatment costs in Poland (art. 144 ust. 1 pkt 2 lit. a). You may attach the policy now; otherwise the voivode can ask for it (art. 106f, at least 14 days to respond).
a.health_insurance.note: A minimum cover of 30,000 EUR appears on a university slide but not in the Act text we checked, so it is not stated here as a rule.
a.means_of_subsistence.title: Proof of means to live on, return travel and study costs
a.means_of_subsistence.detail: Bank statements, a scholarship letter or a sponsor's declaration. The Act requires enough money for living costs, return travel to your home country and the studies, with monthly means above the social-assistance income threshold after housing costs (art. 144 ust. 1 pkt 2 lit. b, ust. 1a).
a.means_of_subsistence.note: The exact euro or zloty threshold is set outside the Act and changes, so it is not hard-coded here.
a.tuition_payment.title: Proof of tuition payment for the semester or year (paid programmes only)
a.tuition_payment.detail: Required by art. 144 ust. 1 pkt 1 lit. b if your studies are paid, whether you start or continue.
a.accommodation.title: Proof of accommodation (rental agreement or dormitory contract)
a.accommodation.detail: The Act does not list accommodation as a condition for a study permit, but your housing cost is deducted when your means are assessed (art. 144 ust. 1a, 1b), so the contract supports the amount you declare in section E.V.
a.accommodation.note: Not mandatory for studies; offices may still ask for it.
a.return_travel.title: Return travel cost
a.return_travel.detail: No ticket is required. The Act only requires that your means cover the cost of returning, which your bank statements show.
fee.stamp_duty_study: Stamp duty for a temporary residence permit (studies)
